title: Alliance-Departments
content:
## Foreign Affairs

Foreign Affairs, also called FA, is an alliance department responsible for alliance dealings with other alliances. Widely regarded as the most important department, FA keeps their alliance in a favorable position in Orbis by maintaining good allies and a good reputation. FA is also involved in facilitating and creating wars and peace treaties.

## Internal Affairs

Internal Affairs, also called IA, is an alliance department responsible for its member’s activity, enjoyment, and other internal factors. IA is responsible for bringing in new applicants, processing those applicants, and ensuring the activity of their members. IA also deals with other government operations which do not fall into any other department.

## Economic Affairs

Economic Affairs, also called Economics or EA, is an alliance department responsible for the alliance’s economics. EA is responsible for ensuring that its members are using efficient city builds, infra and land amounts, and the right projects. EA also ensures that the alliance’s bank is stable and gives grants to alliance members.

## Military Affairs

Military Affairs, also called Milcom, Defence, or MA, is an alliance department responsible for the alliance’s military. MA is responsible for coordinating their alliance during wartime and for counter-attacking raids. MA also ensures that their alliance is prepared for any possible war.

## Technical Affairs

Technical Affairs, also called TA, is an alliance department responsible for the alliance’s technology. TA is responsible for coding bots and scripts to enhance their alliance’s ability and improve the quality of life for their members. TA may also be responsible for ensuring that any third-party bots are safe for use.

TA is a minor department that not all alliances have but some still do. In those that don’t have a TA department, the job is usually a part of either Internal Affairs or Economic Affairs.

title: Alliance-Ranks
content:
## Leader/2iC

The Leader of an alliance has complete control over the alliance. This ranges from maintaining relationships with other alliances to promoting government officers and much more. Some alliances also have a Second in Command (2iC) who assists the leader in their duties.

How people are appointed to these positions differs between alliances.

## High Government

Every alliance has a High Government to manage the alliance. The members of the high government are the heads of their respective [departments](https://politicsandwar.com/pwpedia/article/Alliance-Departments) and are responsible for working with other departments and advising the leader. Some consider high government to also include the Leader and 2iC but others consider high government to be just the department heads.

How people are appointed to high government differs between alliances but people usually serve in low government first.

## Low Government

Alliances have a set of officers in low government who are responsible for assisting the high government in the day-to-day duties of their departments. In some alliances, there is a similar level of Mid Government made up of slightly more senior members of government.

How people are appointed to low government differs between alliances but they are usually active and helpful members.

title: Alliance-Positions
content:
In each alliance, there can be an infinite amount of positions with a maximum of 9 levels. These each have customizable permissions, ranks, and names. Four are default positions that cannot have their permissions other than their name and rank edited. These are:

1. Leader, at level 9, with complete control over the alliance.
2. Heir, at level 8, with the same permissions as the leader and the ability to promote themselves to Leader.
3. Officer, at level 5, with permissions to assist with managing the day-to-day operations of the alliance. And;
4. Member, at level 3, with no governmental permissions.

There is also the applicant position, with no rank nor permissions, for those applying to join.

There are 15 permissions:

* View Bank
* Withdraw Bank
* Change Permissions
* See Spies
* See Reset Timers
* Tax Brackets
* Post Announcements
* Manage Announcements
* Manage Applicants
* Remove Members
* Edit Alliance Info
* Manage Treaties
* Manage Market Share
* Manage Embargoes
* Promote Self to Leader

title: tax-brackets
content:
## Tax brackets

Tax Brackets are how you manage your funds in an alliance. In alliances, each person automatically pays a portion of their income to the alliance. Different alliances have different tax brackets, with differing rates.

Each Tax Bracket has a Monetary and Resource percent, corresponding to the percent of money or resources taken from the member. For instance, a 70% Monetary Tax Rate and 40% Resource Tax Rate (commonly abbreviated as 70/40) will take 70% of a nation’s monetary income and 40% of the resources a nation makes every turn.

## Tax Bracket Management

To set up a tax bracket, simply navigate to the Taxes page (https://politicsandwar.com/alliance/id=[ALLIANCE\_ID]&display=taxes) by clicking “Bank” then clicking “Taxes.” To create a new bracket, type the name of the bracket and the bracket tax rates under “Create New Bracket”, and then create the bracket. It will, by default, have no one on it.  
You can also change the bracket’s name, tax rates, and simply delete the tax bracket with the sections under “Change Member’s Tax Bracket.”

### Permission to Change Taxes

In order to view tax brackets and change them, a member nation must have Bank Access permissions. These permissions are equivalent to the permissions necessary to Withdraw funds from the alliance bank.

### Default Tax Bracket

Every alliance has a tax bracket called the Default tax bracket. The Default bracket is where new members are automatically placed when accepted into an alliance. The Default tax bracket cannot be renamed or deleted.

## Moving People to/from Tax Brackets

To move someone to a tax bracket, you can navigate to “Change Member’s Tax Bracket,” select their nation from the dropdown menu, select the new bracket you want to move them to, then update their bracket. At the bottom of the page, you will also see an option to bulk-move members by city count.

### Deleting Tax Brackets

When a tax bracket is deleted, any members remaining in that bracket are automatically transferred to the Default tax bracket.

## Tax Bracket Viewing

Each bracket has its own table to show all members on the tax bracket. You can find these under the list of all brackets by clicking the link “View Nations”. You can also find it by filling in the blanks in the following link: https://politicsandwar.com/index.php?id=15&tax\_id=[BRACKET\_ID]

**NOTE: Gray Nations are not taxed, regardless of what tax bracket they're in.**

title: how-to-send-message-through-the-api
content:
This is a how-to article for sending messages to players through the Politics and War API.

### Overview

The API endpoint to send messages through is: at <https://politicsandwar.com/api/send-message/>

### Parameters

This API endpoint accepts a POST request with the following parameters:

**key** : This is your API key, found on the account page.

**to** : This is the Nation ID of the recipient. Note that this is not the leader name like in normal messaging.

**subject** : This is the subject of the message. This cannot be null, and can be up to 50 characters in length.

**message** : This is the body of the message. You can use HTML to format your message.

### Response

An example of a successful response from the server looks like:

> {
>
>    "success": true,
>
>    "recipient": "196880",
>
>    "subject": "test"
>
> }

### Errors

Here are a list of errors you may experience and why you may receive them.

#### Invalid API Key

If you do not include a valid API key with your request, you will see the message:

> {
>
>    "success": false,
>
>    "general\_message": "Invalid API key."
>
> }

#### Self Message

If you try to send a message to yourself, you will see the message:

> {
>
>    "success": false,
>
>    "general\_message": ["You cannot send a message to yourself."]
>
> }

#### Recipient Does Not Exist

You must identify a primary recipient by their nation ID. If that ID does not exist, you will see the following message:

> {
>
>    "success": false,
>
>    "general\_message": ["The recipient does not exist. Using this API endpoint, you must send messages to players by their Nation ID rather than their leader name."]
>
> }

#### No Subject

If you do not include the subject field, you will see the following message:

> {
>
>    "success": false,
>
>    "general\_message": ["You must include a subject in your message."]
>
> }

#### No Message Body

If you do not include the message field, you will see the following message:

> {
>
>    "success": false,
>
>    "general\_message": ["You did not include a message body."]
>
> }

title: what-is-the-api
content:
The term **API** stands for **Application Programming Interface**, which you’ve probably never heard of. The best way to think of it is like this. There’s the GUI (Graphical User Interface), you’ve probably heard of that, and the API. The GUI is some nice text and images and is designed for users (you) to interact with. The API on the other hand, is essentially text and some internet communication that is designed for computers to interact with and receive data in the most efficient format possible.

The P&W API is composed of a patchwork of versions and webpages developed over the course of the entire game. For historical purposes I’ll mention that v1 and v2 exist, however v3 should be used for all new projects going forward. v3 provides a much better interface as well as massive amounts of additional data and functionality.  
If you’re interested in learning more about the API, head on over to the Politics and Programming Discord server to ask any questions!

## How to use the API

So now that you know what an API is, you’re probably asking yourself “Why should I care?” It’s a good question, why should you? Well, if you’ve ever interacted with the community on Discord you’ll find lots of wonderful Discord bots and various spreadsheets to help with the game, all of that is powered through the API. The API makes it really easy to, say, get the amount of soldiers on every nation in an alliance, or the amount of cities each member has. You could spend an hour clicking through the member list and recording the data, or you perform a simple query in a programming language and run with it that way!

The API is best served as a tool to make your life, and the lives of everyone else, much easier. It makes it really easy to get important information without having to leave Discord, and to get information in ways that the game simply doesn’t provide. Not only that, but use of the other programming features in conjunction with the API allows really awesome things to arise, like banking systems for alliances!

**NOTE: Use of the API to fully automate gameplay is NOT ALLOWED and WILL result in punishment from the moderation team. Actions to interact with the game should be confirmed or initiated by a user, NOT done automatically on a loop or in response to a change in the game.**

## The GraphQL API

If you want to play around with how to shape your requests, you can use the playground:

<https://api.politicsandwar.com/graphql-playground>

It’s important that you append ?api\_key=xxxxxx to the request url (towards the top of the page, but not the page url itself). If you fail to do this, you will be met with errors about the client being unable to reach the server and/or errors about the api key being entered incorrectly. Please note that you have to use your own API key, instead of xxxxxx. Your API key can be found on the bottom of your account page: https://politicsandwar.com/account/

In order to see type details and arguments, you can press the “docs”-button on the right-hand side of the playground.

title: api-faq
content:
**What are the headers for API v3?**

* **X-RateLimit-Reset-After** - The number of seconds until the rate limit resets.
* **X-RateLimit-Limit** - The maximum number of requests per rate limit period.
* **X-RateLimit-Remaining** - The remaining number of requests before the rate limit is reached. If this reaches zero you should wait the number of seconds in X-RateLimit-Reset-After before attempting another request.
* **X-RateLimit-Reset** - The unix timestamp at which point the rate limit resets.
* **X-RateLimit-Interval** - The length of the rate limit period in seconds.

**What are the headers for the mutation apis?**

* **X-Api-Key** - The API key intended to be used for the mutation
* **X-Bot-Key** - The Mutation key to validate mutation request

title: Basics-of-Internal-Affairs
content:
* Internal Affairs, also known as IA, is a department of an alliance’s government that focuses on the internal aspects of the alliance and its members.
* Internal Affairs works towards ensuring that all members are active in the alliance with a level of competency set. They also deal with members who have either broken alliance rules, or have made a bad decision.
  + Member Applications
    - IA will handle applications to the alliance by setting up a channel for the applicant so they can conduct the interview themselves or with members who volunteer.
  + Activity Management
    - Members will become inactive whether they forget to log in or become busy. IA will step in to handle the situation by having said member login, having members go into vacation mode if needed, or moving them to applicant to avoid the alliance bank getting looted.
  + Training New Players
    - When a new player is accepted into the alliance, they need to be trained in the different aspects of the game. From raiding inactive nations to earn money, understanding how to manage your nation from projects to city builds, to understanding how war works and preparing them for it. It is IA’s job to have those members trained and ready for their journey into politics and war.
  + Removing Leakers and Troublesome Members
    - There will come a time where you will have members who apply with the intention of leaking alliance ospec, or to cause trouble in the alliance. It is up to IA to deal with those members accordingly by getting to the root of the problem and removing it by kicking said member from the alliance and even attacking their nation if the situation calls for it.
  + Audits
    - IA will do audits to make sure everyone is meeting requirements, whether it’s making sure everyone is meeting infra levels, MMR, proper city builds, and more. Those who refuse to meet requirements or have a tendency to fail these audits must be dealt with accordingly.
* To start your IA department, you’ll want someone who can stand their ground and enforce alliance policy even under scrutiny. You’ll also want to setup an interview section with a way for members to apply and have interview channels setup automatically. Making guides meant for teaching new players is a good idea as well.
* It is recommended to expand your IA gov as your alliance's membership expands. A small alliance with only 10-20 members is easy to manage for one person. But as the alliance grows, setting up a chain of command would be beneficial to remain efficient.

title: Basics-of-War-Strategy
content:
War strategy is an extremely subjective thing in Politics and War, your actions in a war eventually depend on a whole lot of factors that you cannot possibly predict beforehand and most of the time you will be relying on the Milcom department in your alliance for specific instructions.

However, there are certain things that are found to be common in the most common circumstances like:

* Circumstance i - Raiding
  + When you are raiding your priority would be to gain maximum profits at minimum costs and to achieve that you need to prepare even before you declare your wars. The first thing you should do is to change your war policy to Pirate which gives you 40% more loot and then make sure you have max barracks and factories in all your cities.
  + Finding a good target is relatively easier in lower tiers where there is no lack of targets.
    - There are discord bots that can assist with this task but for new players it is better to learn what makes a good target than straight up get a list of ‘good targets’ sorted by an algorithm.
    - If you choose to find one manually, you can do an intel-gathering spy operation and get the exact numbers of resources a nation is holding, if that is not an option, you should look for any recent defeats and what they lost in that defeat and the type of war it was, in most cases that gives you a good idea.
    - In general, you are looking for someone who is not very active, has fewer military units than you, has high infra, and is preferably on Turtle or Guardian war policy.
  + All wars you declare with intent to raid should always be raid type so you get 100% of the potential loot.
  + Since ground attack is the only attack type that gets you immediate cash loot with every attack, you should generally be doing mostly ground attacks, in cases where the enemy has no cash but has high amount of resources or you are competing to get the first beige (victory)  you can also go 5 naval attacks and 3 ground attacks to finish the war slightly sooner, get the highest loot and get your slot freed for another raid. In any other case where it is not feasible to win by all grounds or naval and grounds, you should try to achieve victory by any means possible.
* Circumstance ii - Dealing Damage:
  + There are a number of ways to maximize enemy damage and the most straightforward way is to burn their infrastructure as it not only directly costs them to rebuild, they also lose some revenue until the lost infrastructure is rebuilt. One other way is to kill military units but if you are fighting someone you will be killing units in order to win anyway so that is a given.
  + In order to deal maximum damage you should be declaring attrition type wars. Different attack types destroy different amounts of infrastructure but an airstrike on anything other than infrastructure deals the least damage while naval attack with max number of ships for city count does more damage than any other unit apart from nukes, that have the unique quality of dealing the same amount of infrastructure damage from any city count. Nukes are also a good choice when you simply don’t have enough units to launch successful attacks and that can be a very common occurrence.  
    Ground attacks are somewhere in the middle as they destroy more infrastructure than airstrikes (not targeting infra) but less than navals attacks.
  + Unlike raid wars, you will often need to overlook your own losses in units or fuel costs and just hit as hard as you can with what you have, i.e. going with the unit that you have the most of and using 100% of it, sometimes even losing wars just to deal some damage.
  + There will be common cases when the enemy will not have enough infrastructure to destroy and in those cases you should not bother choosing attrition as your war type, the most damage you can deal in such a case is killing as many units as you are able to and stealing as much of their resources as you can.
* Circumstance iii
  + Coordination:
    - If you are part of an alliance in this game, sooner or later you will find yourself in a large-scale alliance war. Alliances generally have a department called MilCom for alliance-wide war strategy and coordination and they will guide you through your specific role in the war. This is an attempt to give you a general idea of how things usually work, you should always prioritize commands from your MilCom over this.
  + Offensive:
    - If you are starting a war, chances are you will start with what we call a ‘blitz’ which basically means declaring a large number of wars on an enemy coalition within a very short period of time, generally right before the server ‘daychange’ at UTC-0.
    - You should have your targets assigned by your MilCom beforehand and some first-day instructions, it is best to neutralize potential threats first i.e. active people with max aircraft. Once you have dealt with planes you can move to ground and finally to navy, if needed.
    - If your alliance/coalition intends to fight for multiple rounds, you will need to practice beige discipline too, which means intentionally not winning a war or even taking a loss if required, not giving enemy beige time and allowing them to rebuild.
  + Defensive:
    - It is very rare for alliances to be able to make a full recovery from a blitz and launch a successful counter-attack but it is not impossible, although it does require insane coordination and a swift response.
    - If you have been blitzed, you should try to launch your counterattacks as soon as you are able to while you still have units, down-declare (declaring on someone with score lower than you) on active combatants, rebuild lost planes and then dogfight, if things are perfectly in your favour there is a very small chance this will give you a fighting chance.
    - Another ancient strategy is to declare on rogue pirates and get them to beige you and then use that beige time to rebuild military units and launch a counterattack, though this may not work if the enemy has a good tiering advantage over you and you may again end up losing all units.
    - When there is no hope for turning the tide of war you will be relying on ‘guerilla tactics’ in attempts to make the war as costly as possible for your enemy. This is done by finding weak targets in the enemy coalition and doing coordinated hits or going solo on enemies with very high infrastructure and dropping nukes and missiles.

title: Basics-of-Econ
content:
* Econ, also known as Economics, is a department of an alliance’s government that focuses on the economic aspects of the alliance and its resources.
* Econ will work towards setting taxes, setting build codes both old and new, calculate how much money is needed to rebuild the alliance after a war, handle the offshore, and overall balance the alliance's budget to ensure its survival.
* Growth Programs  
  + Growth Programs are essential to an alliance's prosperous growth which is why Econ will put a good amount of focus in this area.
  + Loans  
    - Loans are the easiest growth program to setup. It’s best to only allow loans to nations that have been in the alliance for a long time since you don’t want people leaving with loans. It is also best to set a limit based on said nation's economic situation since you don’t want a city 5 nation taking out a loan they can’t pay off in time.
  + Grants  
    - Grants are used to help relieve or help a nation get their next city or a certain project. Most grants are focused towards smaller nations by helping them get milcom-related projects, though larger alliances have the ability to extend that to mid-sized nations.
  + City Circles  
    - City Circles are groups of alliance members who put their income into a pool to buy cities quicker. The profit comes from (said cities income \* days they would have waited to get it). Some alliances have players run it while others have econ run it. No matter how it is run, Econ needs to make sure the funds are used responsibly.
* Rebuild  
  + The biggest cost for a nation after a war is rebuilding infra. Which is why it is Econ’s job to help relieve those nations by rebuilding infra to a certain point. There are a variety of ways to calculate rebuild but most with some alliances having a one-level rebuild while others will have a tiered rebuild. With a one-level rebuild, everyone has their infra built up to let’s say 2k infra, while tiered rebuild is focused on rebuilding nations based on their city tiering with bigger nations getting more infra. Do not be afraid to put everyone on rebuild taxes if the cost is higher than what the rebuild fund can support.
* Setting Taxes  
  + Taxes are what keep the alliance alive and allow for econ to run their different programs. Taxes can be set up in a variety of ways whether your alliance runs 100/100 taxes on everyone or a tiered tax. You’ll want to find a balance between covering the costs of your programs and room for your members to grow. Some alliances have different tax brackets for nations to opt into, some have a single tax that is applied to everyone, but the most popular way of taxing is tiered taxing. Tiered taxing encourages nations to grow into higher tiers and keeps the bigger nations happy since they will have more economic room. You’ll also have to consider resource taxes as well since resources are needed for funding grants. Some alliances tax more money and don’t tax resources, allowing for members to sell their resources to the alliance while others alliances will run an even tax on money and resources. It’s really up to Econ and what is the most comfortable way for them to run it.
* Setting build code  
  + When it comes to maximizing growth, making sure your members are on the most efficient city builds. Generally you will have 3 builds. One build for raiding, one build for commerce, and one build for commerce and manufacturing. You will want your members to switch builds as they grow from raiders to being more self-sufficient. For raiding builds, you only need your raiders to have enough infra to build barracks and tanks and to power them. For manufacturing builds, you will want to have a nation start producing manufactured resources based on what continent their nation is on. Make sure they get the project to boost said resource production. For commerce builds, you will want said nation to reach max commerce which is usually 100% until they get the projects to increase it while also running 0% disease to maximize income while also adding manufacturing improvements as well.
* Offshoring  
  + One of the most important parts of running Econ is protecting its resources by offshoring. To setup an offshore, make a new alliance and make sure to label it as an extension of your alliance by either setting up a prot treaty and or saying this alliance is an extension of said alliance. In the case where you are slotted or you are about to lose wars while in the offshore, have a trusted gov member make a new offshore, and then you will transfer the contents of the first offshore to the 2nd offshore. Make sure it is alliance-to-alliance, otherwise your bank contents will get leaked.
* To setup Econ, you will want someone who is good with numbers, like an accountant of sorts. Setting up sheets to keep track of taxes and holdings is a must-need. It is also a good idea to setup Econ and build guides for your membership as well.
* Econ is a small branch in gov so there is no reason to have a large group since you only need 2-3 people at most. So it’s best to setup a succession line.

title: Basics-of-Milcom
content:
* Milcom is a department of an alliance’s government that focuses on the militaristic side of the alliance.
* Milcom will coordinate wars that the alliance is in, set MMR requirements, set Warchest requirements, deal with raiders attacking the alliance, protect the bank, and help new members with questions they have.
  + War coordination
    - There is a lot of pre-planning before an offensive war even begins. Milcom and/or the alliance’s leader will usually consult with other alliances on beige policy, distribution of targets, and when the war will be declared. For defensive wars, there isn’t much planning since there is little time to prepare after being attacked without notice. But most of the coordinating will be focused on maximizing damage dealt to the enemy and eventually a counterblitz.
  + Dealing With Raiders
    - Eventually you will have some nations attack your alliance to get some juicy loot whether that be from an applicant or an inactive member. It is milcom’s job to prevent pirates from looting members and potentially the bank. Best way to deal with them is to send counters and have the pirates pegged down to where they realize it’s best to not hit your alliance anymore.
  + Protecting The Bank
    - If a member is gonna lose their war, or the alliance is in a global war, it is best to move all the money and resources from the alliance bank to an offshore to protect it from being looted (it is recommended that all government members with bank access should know how to offshore).
  + MMR and Warchest Requirements
    - MMR
      * MMR stands for Minimum Military Requirements. MMR is defined by 4 numbers, which stand for the number of military improvements to have in all cities: first one Barracks, 2nd one Factories, 3rd Hangars, and 4th Drydocks. For MMR, you want to set a balance to where your members can prosper during peacetime and be able to quickly militarize if a war may be happening. The best way is by how frequent your wars are, and how fast your members can militarize.
    - Warchests
      * For Warchests, you should have a warchest that can last you and your alliance through war with a blockade. Most alliances have a city count-based system where you have a base amount of resources times the number of cities said member has (3000 munitions \* city count).
* To set up your milcom department, you will want someone who is experienced with the war system in politics and war and can handle the stress of managing multiple members and their wars. It’s also a good idea to have an area setup for milcom gov to communicate with each other and to make war rooms to coordinate wars with members.
* For Milcom gov, it is best to expand the department with your membership since having 1-2 people handling 70 members during war is not a good idea.

title: Basics-of-Foreign-Affairs
content:
* Foreign Affairs, also known as FA, is a department of an alliance’s government that focuses on the external aspects of the alliance.
* Foreign Affairs works towards setting up the alliance diplomatically with other alliances. They also handle negotiations whether they are for peace, treaties, and etc.
  + Setting Up Embassies
    - Setting up embassies with other alliances is the first step to establishing basic relations with other alliances. It’s a chance for you to get to know the other alliance's gov, and a chance for them to know your gov if they return the favour (do note that some alliances may refuse to create an embassy if your alliance isn’t notable in any capacity).
  + Treaties
    - Whether you are a new alliance, or an established alliance, you are going to need allies to defend you. FA will go out and try to either find a protector if the alliance is small or sign a formalized MDP or MDoAP treaty with another alliance or sphere. It’s always best to go after alliances/spheres that you have a good relationship with or one’s where their politics match with yours.
  + Negotiations
    - When it comes down to peace deals or treaties, there is always negotiation involved so that both parties are satisfied with the terms.
  + Treaties
    - Treaty Negotiations already have a set framework with terms like 72 hour notices, intelligence sharing, mutual defense, and etc. There’s not much work to be done with setting up terms, but you should make sure that those terms are in the treaty.
  + Peace Negotiations
    - When negotiating for peace, terms will be imposed based on the success/failure of the war. If your alliance is on the winning side, then FA will have a bit of leeway to impose some terms. If your alliance is on the losing side, then FA will have to accept some terms they don’t like. There are some lines that should never be crossed such as imposing disbandment of alliances, treaties, and/or spheres will make said alliance's reputation look bad and will most likely get them rolled for it. A good idea is to look at peace terms of the past to have a good grasp of how peace terms work in the game.
* To start your FA department, you will want someone who knows the politics well, is willing to engage in conversations with others, and has a reputation of being competent. You’ll then want to setup an area to host embassies whether on your alliance discord server or somewhere else. After that, you’ll need to introduce yourself to your allies or your protector's allies and eventually to other spheres.
* When it comes to FA gov, you really only need a succession line for FA gov. FA will usually have a team of members to talk in embassies to your alliance with FA low gov and mid gov.

title: Disease
content:
Disease decreases your population which affects your income and military unit recruitment, making it important to keep in check. Disease increases with a higher Population Density and through Pollution. You can decrease disease directly by building Hospitals or indirectly by buying more Land. Indirectly you can decrease disease by decreasing Pollution. Disease can never be zero without having a hospital.

title: Land
content:
**Land** is the space your city has. As you increase land, your **Population** will spread out, decreasing **Population Density** and reducing **Disease** in your city. **Food** is also produced at a rate that is tied to land, the more land you have, the more food each **Farm** will be produced.

Much like **Infrastructure**, Land has a bulk discount; in 500s. You can further reduce land costs via the **Rapid Expansion** domestic policy and projects like **Arable Land Agency** (**ALA**).

content:

title: Infrastructure
content:
Infrastructure is one of the basic building blocks of your city. It directly affects your base Population. Infrastructure also provides improvement slots to build Improvements in your cities at one slot per 50 infrastructure, Improvements you build in these slots remain functioning even if you lose the slots by losing infrastructure but you cannot rebuild a lost Improvement if you don’t have an empty improvement slot. To make the best use of buying infrastructure, **only** buy it in batches of 100s, as that is where the bulk discount is the highest.

With the Urbanization domestic policy, infrastructure costs are reduced 5%. You can also reduce infrastructure costs through projects like **Centre for Civil Engineering** (**CCE**).

title: how-to-delete-a-city-in-politics-and-war
content:
Players can delete their own cities in the online game Politics and War. To do so, they must first sell the infrastructure down to 0.01 in the city they wish to delete. This may require destroying improvements in the city first.

Once a city has reached 0.01 infrastructure, an option on that city page will appear to delete the city. Deleting a city is not reversible, and does not refund you the cost of the city. The first city cannot be deleted.

| **Term** | **Definition** | Contextual Use Case |

| Sheepy/Alex | The game creator/admin |  |
| P&W / PnW | Politics And War |  |

| AA | Alliance Affiliation (shorthand for alliance) | I’ve been in a lot of **AA**s since I started playing. |
| C[Number] | Shorthand to describe how many cities a nation has | I can’t wait to be a **C30** |

| Color Bloc | A color that nation can set itself to | I wasn’t able to log on for a week so I need to switch my **color bloc** off of gray. |

You can learn more about VIP Status [here](https://politicsandwar.com/pwpedia/article/vip-status). | I really miss having a leader portrait and a nation anthem so I am going to buy a credit and buy **VIP status** again. |

## Alliance Terms

| **Term** | **Definition** | **Contextual Use Case** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Leader | The leader of the alliance | I would wait for our **leader** to post an announcement before you make any rash decisions. |
| 2ic | Second in command, above high gov but below leader. Will typically take duty if the leader isn't around in their charge | I think once I retire as leader, I am going to have my **2ic** take over. |
| High gov | Alliance officials in a position of high authority, influence and responsibility within their alliance. Typically department leaders. | He’s high gov, he definitely speaks for his alliance. |

An alliance may have a relatively high or low overall tiering, and may be focussed more-or-less narrowly into one tier, or be spread out among all or certain tiers. | Our tiering is extremely low, we’re all a bunch of c10s. |

title: how-do-rewarded-ads-work
content:
Rewarded Ads offer a voluntary way for you to view advertisements that support the game in exchange for receiving some money in the game. At the time of writing, you can receive up to $2,000,000 per day for your nation from watching Rewarded Ads, at $80,000 per ad watched.

To use Rewarded Ads, click the link “[Rewarded Ads](https://politicsandwar.com/rewarded-ads/)” in the sidebar (or mobile menu) under the **Nation** heading.

Once on that page, you will be able to click the button that says “Begin Rewarded Ad ($80,000)” which will begin loading the video ad. It may take a few seconds to load.

Once the ad is loaded, you will need to watch the whole ad. Sometimes, a “Skip” button will appear (like on a YouTube video) but if you skip the ad, you will not receive the reward in-game. When the ad is finished, it will automatically close out and you will see a notification that you have completed the rewarded ad and have been credited the $80,000 bonus. If you refresh the page, you will see that you have received a notification detailing this as well, and the money will have been added to your inventory.

title: how-to-fix-broken-score-graphs
content:
Are you experiencing an issue where your nation score over time and nation score component graphs are not displaying? While this is an uncommon issue, it has happened frequently enough that we have written this article to explain how to fix it. While we know how to fix it, it is still a mystery as to what causes it exactly.

This issue occurs when a user embeds an image directly into their nation description (or alliance description) through the text editor. Sometimes (and it is not clear what the issue is) this causes the graphs to break. Usually there is just one embedded image that causes the issue.

To troubleshoot and fix, it is best to go through your nation description and remove each image one at a time and re-save until you can identify which image is causing the problem. Once you have identified the problem image, the best solution is to upload that image to an image hosting site, and then insert it via URL instead of uploading it directly or copying and pasting it. To do that, use the “down arrow” next to the image button on the text editor toolbar. Paste in the URL where your image is hosted, and then it should embed like before. Save, and your score graphs should now be working properly.

There are a number of sites where you can upload and host your image. If you use Discord, that is a good alternative. Other options include: [snipboard.io](https://snipboard.io) and [postimages.org](https://postimages.org/).

To get the direct link to your image, right click in your browser and select the option like “Copy Image Address”. It should look something like: https://politicsandwar.com/uploads/1d1fb488e138835e20aebb171662049f13ba8eb3200x112509.png where it contains a “.png”, “.gif”, “.jpg”, or “.jpeg” extension at the end.

***Note:** This issue may exist as well for alliances, and may also cause the “Propose New Treaty” button to not work on Alliance pages.*

title: Improvement-Categories
content:
### Power Plants: Introduction

Power plants are how you power your city. You can build as many power plants as you want.  
Many plants require resources to function, and some make pollution. However, without power, your city may not function properly.

### Raw Improvements: Introduction

Raw Resources are things your nation can produce directly, without any power needed. These are the base elements of manufactured goods. Generally, you can only build ten Mines per city as a maximum. There are two exceptions: Food and Uranium — you can have up to twenty Farms per city and you can have up to five Uranium Mines per city.  
Raw Improvements also have a stacking bonus; the more of one type of mine you have, the more of that resource you make, with a maximum of a 50% bonus. Raw Resources differ based on continent. Below is a chart of which resources you can produce, depending on the continent.

**![pvIVefaH09vt09A4XOh4WYjh8PB_4c70FN0aaDncOtL4VF1ow2SO1gHfBoJMmZE9DXNSyizRLGgfOUlECaGHJu4UoNGEd1SR8GZ0_0EVNOD5pQu14HDQHRraiTAm7BpCJ2XcFV7OGRoTdcTSmUutjYyrRJ3lUC3-Ny2yeOSNVIizR_oDTMAk1dx5r0jKEg](https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/pvIVefaH09vt09A4XOh4WYjh8PB_4c70FN0aaDncOtL4VF1ow2SO1gHfBoJMmZE9DXNSyizRLGgfOUlECaGHJu4UoNGEd1SR8GZ0_0EVNOD5pQu14HDQHRraiTAm7BpCJ2XcFV7OGRoTdcTSmUutjYyrRJ3lUC3-Ny2yeOSNVIizR_oDTMAk1dx5r0jKEg)**

### Manufacturing Improvements: Introduction

Manufacturing Improvements produce Manufactured Resources from Raw Resources. They require power to function, and are much more profitable than raw resources due to the increased output. However, they produce a lot of pollution, so watch out!  
Manufacturing Improvements are offered regardless of continent, and you can have a maximum of 5 of each type of Manufactured Improvement per city.

Like Raw Improvements, these also have a stacking bonus, with a maximum of 50%.

### Civil Improvements: Introduction

Civil Improvements affect certain statistics of your city and as a whole, make life better for your citizens. All but the Police Station reduce disease, either directly or inadvertently through reducing pollution.

As you reduce pollution, disease decreases, but if you go below 0 pollution, reducing pollution further won’t have an effect on disease.

### Commerce Improvements: Introduction

Commerce Improvements increase the commerce percentage of your nation, which allows you to make more money. With a high disease, this will be less effective.

### Military Improvements: Introduction

Military Improvements allow you to build units for your nation. They create space, and the more you have, the more units you’ll be able to build. Most alliances have a Minimum Military Requirement (MMR) based off of these improvements, usually formatted as follows:

* # of barracks/# of factories/# of planes/# of drydocks
* For example, full military improvements would be 5/5/5/3 or 5553.

title: july-2025-update
content:
## Military Research Changes

The Cost side of the module has been renamed to ‘Efficiency’ Research, which now gives increased daily unit purchasing. While upkeep reduction has moved to the Capacity side. All research now also contributes to nation score, with 4 points per air upgrade, 3 for ground upgrades, and 2 for naval upgrades. 

## New Colors and Formula

Four new color blocs have been added to the game; They are Mint, Gold, Lavender and Turquoise. And all colors now calculate their bonus considering both the revenue of all nations on the color and also the total number of new players on the color. The exact formulas are available below.

> Turn Bonus Cap = (Average daily monetary revenue \* 18 /Total Nations) (18 is the number of colors)
>
> Growth Bonus = MIN( ( (Average Daily Monetary Net Revenue of all nations on color \* 0.75) / all Nations on Color), Turn Bonus Cap)
>
> Recruit Bonus = MIN((Total Nations <c21 on Color \* 10/Total Nations <c21) ,1)\* Turn Bonus Cap
>
> Final Turn Bonus = Growth Bonus + Recruit Bonus
>
> Nations in beige, gray, VM, or not in an alliance are excluded from all formulas.

## Treasures

Eight treasures have been added, two per new color. Also there have been a few changes to eligibility for spawning new treasures.

* There are no longer any continent restrictions.
* Alliance and Nation Colors must match to be eligible.
* A nation must have been on a color for at least 30 days to be eligible.

## Miscellaneous

### Project Slots

Project slots are now awarded every 4000 infra, a reduction from the previous 5000.

### Nuclear Power Plants

Nuclear Power Plants now consume 0.25 uranium per 1000 infra each turn, increased from the previous of 0.2 uranium for the same.

### New Themes

Also the game has two new themes available. A very purple theme, ‘Epic Purple’ contributed by Epimetheus. And a Modern style by Monti. These are both available in account settings.

### Projects Page

Finally the projects page has received a small face lift.

## Military Update

We have released a new military update focusing on economic costs, the utility of ships, and the ability to recover in longer alliance wars.

### Military Research

Military Research is the headline feature of this update aimed at providing an alternative way of improving military power outside of buying cities. This new module allows you to purchase permanent upgrades to your unit caps, unit purchase costs, and upkeep costs. This module also comes with 2 new projects. First, the **Military Research Center**, allows you to begin purchasing military research and also increases your project cap by 2. The second, **Military Doctrine** project decreases the cost of buying military research by 5%. Your research can be reset at the cost of 1 credit, refunding your cash investment but not resources. You can find military research on your military page, enjoy!

### Military Page

Speaking of the military page, it has received a major facelift. You can now buy all of your military units on the same page! It also has options for buy all, sell all, and a special option to buy in the standard MMR format used by many alliances.

### Ship Rebalance

Ships have had significant balancing changes made. The most important is they now have 4 attack options similar to planes.

* Target Infrastructure: Does the original infrastructure damages and 30% Reduced Naval Casualties
* Target Ships: Does 30% Reduced Infrastructure and 30% Increased Naval Casualties
* Naval Ground Defense: Does 30% Reduced Infrastructure, 30% Reduced Naval Casualties and Removes Ground Control on immense triumph.
* Naval Air Defense: Does 30% Reduced Infrastructure, 30% Reduced Naval Casualties and removes Air Control on immense triumph.

Additionally all naval battles now have 20% more ship casualties for both sides compared to previously. And finally ships have their operation costs reduced. Gasoline has been reduced from 1.5 to 1 gasoline per ship per battle. With munitions reduced from 2.5 to 1.75 munitions per ship per battle.

### Cost Tweaks

Some units have had their upkeep or purchase costs changed to address economic imbalances between units.

#### Upkeep

* Ships > Reduced to 3300 during peace & 5000 during war (Previously 3375 & 5062.5)
* Planes > Increase to 750 during peace & 1000 during war (Previously 500 & 750)

#### Purchase Costs

* Plane cost increased from 5 aluminum per plane to 10 aluminum per plane
* Nuke cost increased to 1000 aluminum, 500 gasoline, 500 uranium
* Missile cost increased to 150 aluminum, 100 gasoline, 100 munitions

### Beige Buff

Players in beige with no active wars will see an increase in the number of soldiers, tanks, aircraft, and ships they can recruit per day by 15%. This effect is additive with the Propaganda Bureau project. The goal of this change is to allow knocked down players to return to fighting more easily.

title: alliance-treasure-bonus
content:
Alliance Treasure Bonus is a game mechanic that rewards alliances that have nations which possess [Treasures](#).

### How It Works

Alliances by default have a 0% Alliance Treasure Bonus. When alliance members possess treasures in their nations, the entire alliance receives a bonus to their gross income. Alliance Treasure Bonus is calculated using the formula below. Alliance applicants and nations not on the same color as the alliance do not receive this bonus.

### Formulas

*\*All Formulas Are Per Turn Unless Otherwise Noted*

Alliance Treasure Bonus = sqrt(Treasures In Alliance \* 4)

title: daily-login-bonus
content:
The daily login bonus is a reward for being an active player and checking on your nation every day.

### How It Works

Every day that you login, your nation earns a minimum of $500,000. For each day that you consecutively login, you add $500,000 to that amount, up to a maximum of $3,000,000 per day. When you miss a day, you go down two steps, not down to zero. If you consistently log in every day, your nation can earn up to $21,000,000 per week just by being active.

### New Players

New players with nations less than 60 days old have a maximum cap of $6,000,000. They have the same $500,000 minimum, and increment by $500,000 per day.

title: Colour-Trade-Blocs
content:
Colour Trade Blocs are a feature where you decide what colour your nation is on. You want to match your colour with your alliance’s colour, as that will give a bonus depending on the colour.

There are two special blocs: Beige and Grey. You cannot change to either of them, though you will not be taxed on either.

* Beige is for new nations or nations that have just lost a war. On Beige, you get a set $85,000 bonus. When your nation is created, you are given 14 days of time on Beige (Beige Time), and after you lose a war, you are given 2 days of Beige Time, which stacks per war.
* Grey is for inactive nations and gives no bonus. It is not preferable to be on Grey for this reason. You will be moved to Grey after Beige Time expires or if you have been inactive for at least 5 days.

title: Score
content:
Score is generally the main determinant of war and spy ranges. It is determined through Cities, Infrastructure, Projects, Military and Military Research with the following formula:  
Nation Score = (City Count - 1) \* 100 + (Nation Infra Total / 40) + (Project Count \* 20) + ((Soldiers \* 0.0004) + (Tanks \* 0.025) + (Aircraft \* 0.3) + (Ships \* 1) + (Missiles \* 5) + (Nuclear Weapons \* 15)) + (Air Upgrades \* 4) + (Ground Upgrades \* 3) + (Naval Upgrades \* 2) + 10

title: Treasures
content:
Treasures are a feature that increases both your nation and alliance’s income. Your alliance gets a bonus for each treasure it has with this formula:

* square root of; (# of Treasures in the Alliance)\* 4

Your nation’s bonus depends on which treasure you get, varying between 5 and 9 percent.  
You can get a treasure in three ways: Random Spawning, Treasure Trading, and Winning Through War.

Treasures have a set timer, and spawn on a nation depending on continent and/or colour assigned to the treasure. They spawn every 60 days in nations between 15 and 65 percent of the largest nation’s score. You can find all treasures, reset timers, current holders, and parameters for each treasure here: <https://politicsandwar.com/leaderboards/display=treasures>

You can also trade treasures for money here: <https://politicsandwar.com/nation/trade/treasures/>. This will directly give you the treasure if you are buying or give someone else the treasure you have.

Finally, you can win a war against a nation with a Treasure in it, which will give you the Treasure though you have to make sure your nation is not under a blockade when you finish the war.

title: War-Policy
content:
War Policy directly affects how your wars will look like. Different policies can be used in different situations, and you can only change policy once every 60 turns (5 days). Below is a list of war policies with their following modifications.

**Attrition**  
This makes offensive Ground Battles, Airstrikes, and Naval Battles do 10% more Infrastructure Damage. However, you will receive 20% less loot in attacks or end-of-war loot.  
Generally, this is best used when trying to cause as much damage as possible. If you do not care about loot and want to just do infrastructure damage. Attrition is the one for you.

**Turtle**  
On the other side, Turtle looks to minimise infrastructure damage. It acts in the reverse of Attrition, decreasing infrastructure damage taken from Ground Battles, Airstrikes, and Naval Battles by 10%, but allowing you to lose 20% more loot.  
This is best used when you have nothing but infrastructure left, and want to protect it.

**Blitzkrieg**  
Blitzkrieg essentially looks to have quick benefits. For the first 12 turns (24 hours) after switching, your nation does 10% more infrastructure damage and casualties in Ground Battles, Airstrikes, and Naval Battles. However, when you are declared on while having this policy, the attacker starts with an extra Military Action Point.  
If you’re looking for short-term benefits, this is the policy for you.

**Fortress**  
While Blitzkrieg speeds up damage, Fortress looks to slow it down. This war policy decreases both the attacker’s and defender’s starting Military Action Points by 1.  
Fortress is if you want to slow down wars as much as possible, more or less.

**Moneybags**  
Moneybags is concerned about money. It decreases loot stolen by 40%, but at the expense of an extra 5% infrastructure damage taken.  
If you are concerned about having loot taken from you, this is the best policy to protect it.

**Pirate**  
The offensive version of Moneybags, Pirate increases the amount of loot stolen by 40%, but gives your nation a double chance to have improvements destroyed in Ground and Naval Battles.  
If you are raiding and don’t care about if improvements are destroyed, then this is the most preferable option for you.

**Tactician**  
Tactician directly targets enemy improvements, doubling the chance to destroy an enemy’s improvements in Ground and Naval Battles. However, if your nation is targeted with Espionage Operations, the saboteur has a 15% greater chance of success.  
If you are directly looking to destroy improvements, Tactician is perfect for you.

**Guardian**  
Guardian protects improvements, acting as the defensive version of Tactician. It halves the chance of having improvements destroyed, but at the expense of losing 20% more loot. This reduction does not work against fixed improvement damage sources such as missiles or nuclear weapons.   
If you are concerned about losing improvements, then this is the best policy for you.

**Covert**  
Covert and Arcane focus directly on spy ops. Covert increases offensive espionage operations’ chances of success by 15%. However, your nation takes 5% more infrastructure damage in Ground Battles, Airstrikes, and Naval Battles.  
If you are looking to do a lot of offensive ops, then Covert is the best policy for you.

**Arcane**  
Finally, Arcane is the defensive version of Covert. With Arcane, an opponent’s chance of succeeding in ops against your nation is decreased by 15%. However, like Covert, your nation takes 5% more infrastructure damage in Ground Battles, Airstrikes, and Naval Battles.

If you are worried about an opponent doing ops on your nation, then Arcane is the best option for you.

title: gross-domestic-product
content:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is a measurement of the wealth and resources generated by a nation over the period of one year.

### Wealth

---

GDP is determined in large part by a nation's net income, or gross income less gross expenses. Factors such as military and other expenses, as well as alliance taxes detract from a nation's GDP.

### Resources

---

The net resources that a nation produces contribute to a nation's GDP, factored in at the current average market prices when GDP is calculated. For this reason, changes in average market prices can change the GDP of a nation, all other factors held constant.

### GDP per Capita

---

GDP per Capita is the average GDP per citizen. A higher GDP per Capita generally indicates that a nation's citizens have a higher quality of life compared to a nation with a lower GDP per Capita.

### Calculation

---

GDP is the summation of a nation's net income per day, as well as the monetary value of net resources produced, multiplied by 365.24. It is calculated and updated each time a nation visits its Revenue page.

### Formula

GDP = (Net Income Daily + (Net Resources Produced Daily \* Average Market Prices)) \* 365.24   
GDP per Capita = GDP / Population

title: Cities
content:
Cities are one of the most key elements of Politics and War. They are at the core of your nation and determine a variety of things.

Cities increase score directly and are worth 75 Score per City. They allow development, including the option to build infrastructure, land, and improvements.

To build a city, you can go to “Cities” and click “Create New City.” That will take you to this link: <https://politicsandwar.com/city/create/.>  
  
The cost of a new city can be calculated using the following formula: Next City Cost = 50000\*(X-1)^3 + 150000\*X + 75000.

To destroy a city, you want to sell Infrastructure and Land down to 0.01, and then you will see an option to delete. You can sell Infrastructure and Land by inputting negative numbers in the buy/sell field.

title: food
content:
**Availability**

* All Continents
* Antarctica has a base 50% reduction in production

**Production**

Farms produce food, and the amount that they produce is dependent upon your city's Land Area. Farms are very cheap to build and operate, and never run out of Food to grow. Each city can have up to 20 Farms.

**Season Affect**

Food is affected by the Game Date. Food Production varies from season to season, depending on which Hemisphere your nation is in.

When your nation's Hemisphere is in **Summer**, you will experience a **20% increase** in Food Production. When your nation's Hemisphere is in **Winter**, you will experience a **20% decrease** in Food Production. During Spring and Fall Food Production remains normal.

The **Mass Irrigation National Project** changes the Food production formula in a way that allows you to grow more Food.

**Uses**

* Feed your population
* If you run out of Food your Gross Income will fall by 33%.
* Soldier upkeep

**Formulas**

* All Formulas Are Per Turn Unless Otherwise Noted
* Normal City Food Production = (City's Land Area / 500) \* Farms
* Mass Irrigation City Food Production = (City's Land Area / 400) \* Farms
* Population's Food Consumption per city per day = ((base\_population)^2) / 125\_000\_000) + (((base\_population) \* (city\_age\_modifier) - base\_population) / 850), where city\_age\_modifier = 1 + max(log(age) / 15, 0)
* Peacetime Soldier's Food Consumption = Soldiers / 9000
* Wartime Soldier's Food Consumption = Soldiers / 6000
* Summer's Seasonal Effect = Food Production \* 1.2
* Winter's Seasonal Effect = Food Production \* 0.8

Ships are used for naval battles, they can only destroy enemy ships, however, they have 50% higher chances of destroying an enemy improvement than a ground battle with an Immense Triumph.

title: Planes
content:
Aircraft or Planes are highly versatile military units built using hangars in game and are used for targeted strikes on the enemy. Within the current norms of warfare in Politics and War they are widely regarded to be the most important military unit and all major alliances prefer to keep the maximum number of planes at all times.

Aircraft are used for airstrikes and can target enemy soldiers, tanks, aircraft, ships, infrastructure, or cash. When you target infrastructure, you cannot select the city, it will automatically target the city with the highest infrastructure. Your aircraft will always kill some enemy aircraft regardless of what you target but you destroy a significantly higher number while also losing less when you specifically target aircraft. Your planes are also vulnerable to enemy tanks in defensive ground battles if the enemy has ground control on you.

Planes cost 5 aluminum and $4000 each to build. Each hanger allows you to build 3 planes per day and can hold 15 planes.

Each plane costs $500 per day in peacetime and $750 per day in wartime.

Planes require 1 munition and 1 gasoline per 4 planes in battles to operate.

title: population-cap
content:
Your rebuy cap and total unit cap are limited by the number of military improvements you have, as well as your population. The formulas below are based on your total unit cap.

Total number of Soldiers = 0.15 x Population

Total number of Tanks = 0.015 x Population

Total number of Aircraft = 0.001 x Population

Total number of Ships = 0.0001 x Population

Population required for Total number of Soldiers = Total Soldiers / 0.15

(20 population per 3 soldiers)

Population required for Total number of Tanks = Total Tanks / 0.015

(200 population per 3 tanks)

Population required for Total number of Aircraft = Total Aircraft / 0.001 OR Total Aircraft x 1,000

(1,000 population per aircraft)

Population required for Total number of Ships = Total Ships / 0.0001 OR Total Ships x 10,000

(10,000 population per ship)

Example:

If you are a C5 (5 cities) nation with 3 drydocks in every city, your maximum number of ships would be 75 ships (excluding military research)

The minimum population required for 75 ships would be 75 / 0.0001 = 750,000

Given that Base Population = Infrastructure \* 100,

Infrastructure = Base Population / 100

750,000 population / 100  = 7,500 infra

7,500 infra / 5 cities = 1,500 infra

This works out to be around 1,500 infra per city for a C5 nation but note that crime and disease reduce your population and city age bonus increases your population, so the exact amount of infra varies.

title: Spies
content:
Spies are espionage units used to conduct espionage operations on an enemy, they do not require any city improvement or national project to be recruited and their recruitment is not affected by the nation's population like other military units. Spies can do several things but perhaps the most important of them is their ability to gather intelligence on an enemy allowing you to see the resources in their nation.

Spies are used for espionage operations allowing you to gather intelligence, sabotage military units, assassinate enemy spies or terrorize civilians. You do not have to be at war with someone to execute an espionage operation on them.

Spies cost $50k each to recruit. You can have a maximum of 50 spies by default, this limit can be increased to 60 with the Intelligence Agency national project which also allows you to recruit 3 spies per day instead of 2 by default. Spy Satellite national project allows you to train an additional spy per day for ‌4 if you already have Intelligence Agency.

Spies cost $2.4k each in upkeep at all times, this amount is not affected by being at war like other military units.

Spies do not cost any resources to operate, however, they require some cash to operate which can vary depending on the number of spies used and the level of safety being used in operation.

title: Nukes
content:
Nuclear weapons or nukes are weapons of mass destruction built using the Nuclear Research Facility and do not require any city improvement. They are best known for their massive infrastructure damage and the radiation that stays after the attack for over a week, keeping the pollution level high in affected cities and thus increasing disease and reducing the population. Nukes are the only military unit that are able to destroy power plants in a city.

Nukes are launched using 12 MAPs on an enemy city of player’s choice, however, nukes don’t let you choose the type of improvements you want to target like missiles. A successful nuclear attack destroys 4 improvements in a city and a significant amount of infrastructure. Enemies with the Vital Defense System national project will have a 25% chance of thwarting a nuclear attack.

Each nuke costs $1.75m, 750 aluminum, 500 gasoline and 250 uranium. There is no limit on how many nukes you can have at once but you can only build one nuke per day. The Nuclear Launch Facility national project allows you to build an additional Nuclear Weapon each day.

Each nuke adds $35k to your daily upkeep cost in peacetime which increases to $52.5k in war time.

Nukes don’t require any resources to be launched.

title: Missiles
content:
Missiles are ranged military units that are built using the Missile Launch Pad national project instead of a city improvement like most other military units. Because of their relative ineffectiveness in conventional warfare in Politics and War they are often used as the last resort. They can target a specific type of improvements which can be a slight edge over other options for you or just another feature depending on what you are using them for.

Missiles are launched with 8 MAPs and you can choose the city and improvements category you want to target. Missiles have a 100% chance of destroying two improvements upon a successful hit and some infrastructure in the targeted city, capped at 300. Enemies with the Iron Dome national project will have a 30% chance of shooting down your launched missiles and they will only lose one improvement if they get hit by a missile.

Spy attacks against missiles have a 25% chance to destroy an additional missile.

Each missile costs $150k, 100 aluminum, 75 gasoline and 75 munitions to build. There is virtually no limit on how many missiles you can have at one point but you can only build two per day by default or three per day with the Space Program national project.

Missiles cost $21k per day each in peacetime and $31.5k per day in wartime.

Missiles do not require resources to be launched.

title: Soldiers
content:
Soldiers are infantry units that are recruited using barracks. They operate with 175% combat value when used with munitions. When defending against an enemy ground attack, soldiers will automatically use munitions if they are available. With offensive attacks, however,  you receive the option to launch an attack without munitions with 100% combat value.

Soldiers are used in ground battles, optionally with tanks, using 3 Military Action Points with each attack and bringing down enemy resistance by 10 if you achieve Immense Triumph.  
Soldiers also bring instant cash loot with each successful ground attack and the potential loot you can gain increases with the number of soldiers sent in battle.

Soldiers cost $5 each to recruit. Each barrack you possess allows you to recruit 1000 soldiers every day and can hold 3000 soldiers.

In peacetime, soldiers cost $1.25 per soldier and 1 unit of food per 750 soldiers per day. In wartime, they cost $1.88 per soldier and 1 unit of food per 500 soldiers per day.

Soldiers only use munitions in wars and will consume 1 unit of munitions per 5000 soldiers in ground battles both defensive and offensive, unless you run out of munitions or choose not to use them in offensive attacks.

title: Tanks
content:
Tanks are heavy armored units built using factories in game. They are used with soldiers for offensive ground attacks, but can still hold on their own without soldiers while defending against an enemy ground attack. Tanks normally have a combat value equal to 40 soldiers without munitions that can be halved against an enemy with Air Superiority on you.

Tanks are used for ground attacks, however, you still need at least 50 soldiers to launch an attack. Tanks significantly increase your ground capabilities, allowing you to loot much more with your ground attacks, destroy much higher amounts of infrastructure and also destroy enemy aircraft if you have Ground Control established.

Tanks cost 0.50 steel and $60 per tank to build. Each factory allows you to build 50 tanks per day and holds a maximum of 250 tanks.

Tanks cost $50 per day in peacetime and $75 per day in wartime.

Tanks use 1 unit of munitions and 1 unit of gasoline per 100 tanks to operate in battles.

title: Nuclear-Attack
content:
Nuclear attack is the most destructive attack type in-game. It requires 12 Military Action Points (MAP) to execute and has a 100% chance of destroying four enemy improvements upon a successful hit. Two of these improvements can be any improvement and the other two can be any non-power plant, non-military improvement. In the event that two such improvements are not available, it can destroy any improvement. A successful hit also reduces enemy resistance by 25, making it the least MAP efficient attack type in-game in terms of “MAP to resistance reduced” ratio. Like missiles, a nuclear attack also lets you choose the city you would like to target but it does not let you choose the type of improvements to target.

Nuclear attacks directly kill a portion of a city’s population and destroy very high amounts of infrastructure in targeted cities, capped at 2000. They also considerably increase pollution levels in that city causing a high disease rate and a low population that decays over the next 10 days.

Vital Defense System national project gives you a 25% chance of thwarting enemy nuclear attacks and reduces the number of non-power plant, non-military improvements destroyed by a nuke by 1.

Fallout Shelter national project decreases damage from nuclear weapons by 10%, fallout length by 25%, and caps the radiation impact on food production at 90%.

Guiding Satellite increases infrastructure damage dealt by Missiles and Nuclear Weapons by 20% as well as destroy an additional improvement.

title: Fortify
content:
Fortification is a defensive military action, the only one as of now. It takes 3 Military Action Points (MAP) to execute and has no effect on your or enemy’s resistance. While fortified your enemy will suffer 25% more casualties in their offensive attacks against you. When fortified, the effect will last until you launch an offensive attack on the enemy, after which it will require 3 more MAPs to reinstate.

While the game allows you to fortify multiple times in a row, the effect will always be the same as one fortify, and it is highly advised not to do that unless you are willingly wasting MAPs.

title: Espionage
content:
An espionage operation is executed using spies. They do not cost Military Action Points and you do not have to be at war with a nation to do a spy operation on them but you can only do a few operations per day, the base limit is one per day which can be increased to two per day with the Intelligence Agency national project. It is the most versatile military action in-game while also arguably being the least effective during war-time depending on scale and extent of the war.

An espionage operation allows you to execute following actions:

1. Gather Intelligence : Allows you to get information about cash and resources (excluding credits) a nation is holding and the number of spies they have.
2. Assassinate Spies : Allows you to assassinate enemy spies.
3. Terrorize Civilians : Allows you to destroy some infrastructure in the city with highest infrastructure.
4. Sabotage Soldiers : Allows you to kill enemy soldiers.
5. Sabotage Tanks : Allows you to kill enemy Tanks.
6. Sabotage Aircraft : Allows you to kill enemy Aircraft.
7. Sabotage Ships : Allows you to kill enemy Ships.
8. Sabotage Missiles : Allows you to destroy 1 enemy missile with a successful spy operation. Spy attacks against missiles have a 25% chance to destroy an additional missile.
9. Sabotage Nuclear Weapons : Allows you to destroy 1 enemy nuclear weapon with a successful spy operation. However you can not destroy a nuclear weapon the same day it was built on.

You can also select the Safety Level of your spy operation from “Quick and Dirty”, “Normal Precautions” and “Extremely Covert” which directly affect the success chances and the cost to execute the operation with the first being the cheapest and last being the costliest.

The Spy Satellite national project increases the damages from successful espionage operations by 50% and decreases the cost of espionage operations by 20%.

Espionage operations are limited by the spy range, which extends from -60% to +150% of your nation's score. This ensures that only similarly sized nations are able to conduct espionage operations on each other. This prevents very large nations from picking on very small nations.

title: Air-Superiority
content:
Air superiority can be achieved by getting Immense Triumph in an airstrike regardless of the units targeted. This halves the combat value of enemy tanks and thus has a significant impact on your subsequent ground battles with tanks, both offensive and defensive.

Similar to ground control and a blockade, air superiority can be removed in 4 ways. You can do an airstrike that gets you anything but an Utter Failure, a third nation can get an Immense Triumph on your enemy with air superiority, or if they lose all their aircraft. The Naval Air Defense attack option for ships would also remove air superiority upon getting immense triumph.

title: Missile-Strike
content:
Missile strikes are targeted artillery strikes. It takes 8 Military Action Points (MAP) to launch a missile and has a 100% chance of destroying two enemy improvements upon a successful hit, also reducing enemy resistance by 18. When you launch a missile you can choose the city to target and type of improvements to destroy, missiles however cannot destroy power plants. Missiles also destroy infrastructure in the targeted city, and the amount of infra a missile can destroy is capped at 350. \*There have been instances where this cap was breached.\*

The Iron Dome national project gives you a 30% chance of blocking missiles launched at your nation and reduces the number of improvements destroyed by a missile by 1.

Guiding Satellite increases infrastructure damage dealt by Missiles and Nuclear Weapons by 20% as well as destroy an additional improvement.

title: Naval-Battles
content:
Naval battles are attacks done with ships, and can only destroy enemy ships and infrastructure, although the amount of infrastructure destroyed is considerably higher than other attacks for the same city count.

You need at least one ship to launch a naval attack with a 100% chance of Immense Triumph against an enemy with no ships.

A naval attack takes 4 Military Action Points (MAP) to execute and can reduce 14 enemy resistance with an Immense Triumph, making it the most MAP efficient attack type in terms of “MAPs to resistance reduced ratio” in-game. An Immense triumph also gets you 15% chance of destroying an enemy improvement and puts your enemy under blockade restricting their ability to trade on the open market and make bank transactions.

A Moderate Success in a naval attack reduces enemy resistance by 11 and a Pyrrhic Victory reduces it by 8.

title: Airstrike
content:
Airstrikes are targeted strikes done using aircraft. An airstrike allows you to target enemy soldiers, tanks, aircraft, ships, infrastructure or money. Your aircraft will always kill some enemy aircraft regardless of what you target in your airstrike, but in a dogfight (airstrike on aircraft) the number is significantly higher. You need at least 3 aircraft to launch an airstrike, which can get you Immense Triumph against an enemy with no aircraft.

This attack type costs 4 Military Action Points(MAP) and with an Immense Triumph, reduces enemy resistance by 12, also achieving air superiority which halves the combat value of enemy tanks in all subsequent ground battles, offensive or defensive. Airstrikes do not destroy enemy improvements.

In an airstrike, a Moderate Success reduces enemy resistance by 9 and a Pyrrhic Victory reduces it by 6.

title: Ground-Battles
content:
Ground battles are attacks done with your ground units. This is the only attack type that involves 2 different military units, soldiers and tanks. This is also the only attack type that gets you cash loot (no resources) with each attack depending on certain factors.

To launch a successful ground attack you need at least 50 soldiers, although it is highly discouraged to use only 50 soldiers since in most cases it will cause an Utter Failure because of enemy population resistance, another feature unique to this attack type where attacking forces also have to face resistance from population, the effect/impact of the resistance is proportional to nation’s population.

This attack costs 3 Military Action Points (MAPs) to execute.

An Immense Triumph with ground reduces enemy resistance by 10, gets you ground control allowing you to destroy enemy aircraft in subsequent ground attacks, and also gives you a 10% chance of destroying enemy improvement. A Moderate Success reduces enemy resistance by 7 and a Pyrrhic Victory reduces it by 4.

title: War-Types
content:
In Politics and War when you declare a war you can choose from 3 different war types:  ‘Ordinary’, ‘Raid’ and ‘Attrition’. These war types affect the damage you deal to your opponent and the loot you gain from the war. The War type can not be changed once a war is declared. Please note that while the war type affects the defender’s attacks differently than the attacker’s, the defending player cannot choose their own war type or change the existing war type.

title: Blockade
content:
A Blockade is initiated by getting an Immense Triumph in a naval attack. Unlike ground control and air superiority, a blockade does not directly affect wars, however, its indirect effects still make it a crucial part of warfare in Politics and War.

A nation with a blockade loses its ability to trade on market and make transactions with an alliance bank, this is useful when you want to stop your enemy from restocking supplies and continuing their war efforts.

A blockaded nation can still redeem a few credits for cash and resources for their nation and will still be able to make alliance to alliance and alliance to other nations transactions if they have the permissions in their alliance. If the blockaded nation does not have multiple blockades on them by different nations, they can also trade with the one nation holding the blockade.

There are 3 different ways to break a blockade:

1. You can break a blockade by doing a naval attack on the nation holding the blockade and getting anything but an Utter Failure, this is arguably the easiest or most viable method, given that you have resources to build enough ships.
2. The second method is having another nation get an Immense Triumph on the nation holding the blockade on you, essentially putting them under blockade now.
3. The third method is destroying all enemy ships by any means possible, also true for cases where the enemy decommissioned their navy themselves.

title: Attrition-War
content:
Attrition war type focuses on dealing infrastructure damage to the enemy. With this war type in an offensive war you deal 100% of the potential infrastructure damage but only loot 25% of the potential loot. As the description suggests, this war type is for wars where your aim is to deal maximum infrastructure damage while losing loot in opportunity cost.

In a defensive attrition war, you deal 100% of infrastructure damage while also taking 50% of the potential loot.

content:

In a defensive raid war, you get 100% of potential loot while also dealing 50% of potential infrastructure damage.

content:

This is true for both the attacks made in a defensive ordinary war and in an offensive ordinary war.

title: Ground-Control
content:
Ground control can be gained by doing a ground attack and getting Immense Triumph on your enemy. Once you have gained ground control, your tanks will kill some enemy aircraft in all subsequent ground attacks as long as you can maintain your ground control. The number of aircraft you destroy depends on the number of tanks you use in your ground attacks.

In order to break enemy ground control on your nation, you need to get anything but an Utter Failure in a ground attack on a nation holding the ground control on you. Alternatively, it can also be broken by a third nation getting Immense Triumph on nation holding ground control on you and gaining ground control on them or destroying all enemy ground units (i.e. Soldiers and Tanks) by any means. The Naval Ground Defense attack option for ships also removes ground control upon getting immense triumph.
